bullets.title: LEAD - CLAUDE CODE 2.1.274 SHIPPED AT 00:12 THIS MORNING AND IT CONTAINS A SECRET-DISCLOSURE FIX ON THE EXACT SURFACE OUR WHOLE ESTATE RUNS ON: MCP ERROR MESSAGES WERE PRINTING CREDENTIALS RESOLVED FROM ${VAR} PLACEHOLDERS IN MCP CONFIGS
bullets.summary: Dateline read at the page: "ashwin-ant released this 17 Sep 00:12". Four things matter. (i) Quoted: "Fixed MCP connection errors and the MCP login tool's description showing secrets resolved from ${VAR} placeholders in MCP configs" - our configs are exactly that shape and connection errors are exactly the text that gets pasted into logs and reports. (ii) A new claude_code.managed_settings_resolved OpenTelemetry event reports managed-settings sources and policy-helper state, with redacted settings and digests behind OTEL_LOG_MANAGED_SETTINGS=1, plus enduser.sub (the IdP subject) in the telemetry Claude Desktop and Cowork send through a gateway - which is the instrument standing item (b) has been waiting on. (iii) Five MCP connection bugs fixed at once: legacy HTTP+SSE servers failing on a 422/4xx first answer; Streamable HTTP calls timing out at ~5 min despite a longer per-server timeout; prompts/resources not refreshing on list-changed without listChanged; 403 insufficient_scope misreported as expired sign-in; and new CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_STARTUP_WAIT_MS. Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry and telemetry-disabled installs now default to the v2 MCP client and MCP 2026-07-28 negotiation. (iv) Two fixes land on the mechanism producing this file: /schedule was saving a routine's prompt without its message role, and cloud routines now skip and retry for up to 72 hours when the owner's GitHub connection is missing instead of switching off at the first failed check. Archive grep: 2.1.274 ZERO, STARTUP_WAIT_MS ZERO, critical memory ZERO across eighty files.
bullets.how: YES - the one item this week with a same-day operational action rather than a reading action. Order: update, then grep our own logs and pasted error text for ${VAR} values leaked by pre-2.1.274 MCP connection errors, then turn on OTEL_LOG_MANAGED_SETTINGS=1 for one session and finally type item (b) against what it actually prints. That last step is a morning's work deferred sixteen times on a premise the vendor removed overnight.

bullets.title: DAY FIVE OF THE AGENT-GOVERNANCE STACK, AND TODAY'S ENTRANT IS SELLING AGAINST TUESDAY'S - COMP AI RAISED $34M TO MAKE COMPLIANCE CONTINUOUS, ON THE EXPLICIT ARGUMENT THAT A POINT-IN-TIME CERTIFICATE GOES STALE THE MOMENT YOU DEPLOY AN AGENT
bullets.summary: Dateline read at the page: 4:00 AM PDT, September 17, 2026. $34M Series A led by Roo Capital and Grand Ventures, $37.5M to date, founded last January by Lewis Carhart (CEO), Claudio Fuentes (COO) and Mariano Fuentes (CTO). Agents draft security policies and collect audit evidence, the platform continuously monitors whether controls are met, and it runs AI-powered penetration testing against codebases and infrastructure. It explicitly does not replace independent audit review and the humans stay: "An agent might draft a policy, for example, but a person still reviews and approves it... As agents take on more consequential actions over time, we believe the level of safeguards and human approval should increase accordingly." The pitch, quoted: "Imagine a company completes its SOC 2 audit and two weeks later deploys a new AI agent that can access customer data, change permissions across an internal system, or introduce a new vulnerability through code deployment. The audit didn't become invalid; it simply wasn't designed to tell you in real time what changed afterward." Archive grep: Comp AI ZERO, Roo Capital ZERO, Grand Ventures ZERO, compliance agent ZERO.
bullets.how: YES - the sequencing is now a five-day argument rather than a list: 14-15 Sep Kurtz (detect), 15 Sep AIUC $40M quarterly certification with insurance (certify), 16 Sep Cohesity rollback of agent memory and config (recover), 15-16 Sep WSO2 open control plane (govern), 17 Sep Comp AI (monitor - the argument that the certify rung decays between stamps). Two funded companies now sell opposite shapes of the same assurance, a periodic stamp versus a continuous signal, and that disagreement is worth more to us than either. For PRAGMA it is a sellable frame we did not have on Tuesday: an AAIR score is a STAMP, every stamp invites Carhart's question about what changed two weeks later, and the flywheel's re-measure cadence is the answer - price and describe it as the monitoring rung, not as a repeat of the audit. Mariano's operational half is the same sentence as yesterday's: you must be able to show what an agent accessed, what it tried to do, and whether it stayed within its boundaries. Our estate cannot currently show any of the three.

bullets.title: THE PLATFORM SHIPPED COMPACTION YOU CONTROL - YOU CHOOSE WHEN IT FIRES, IT RETURNS A SIGNED BLOCK, AND YOU CAN KEEP RECENT TURNS WORD FOR WORD - WHICH IS THE DIRECT ANSWER TO THE FAILURE MODE THIS REPORT DOCUMENTED YESTERDAY
bullets.summary: Read off the vendor's own dated index, entry dated September 14, 2026. The Messages API can now compact a conversation on demand, in beta behind the compact-2026-09-04 beta header: send a top-level compaction parameter, get back a SIGNED compaction block summarising the messages you sent, and on later requests send that block first in place of those messages. Three properties are the point - you choose when, the request can run in the background, and you can keep recent turns word for word after the summary; on models with preserved thinking, the thinking in those kept turns can stay valid. Archive grep: compact-2026-09-04 ZERO, compact on demand ZERO, signed compaction ZERO; compaction hits four files (2026-08-27, 09-04, 09-08, 09-16) and every one is about compaction happening TO us, not about controlling it.
bullets.how: YES, and it retires a standing worry rather than adding one. Yesterday's file recorded that compaction silently drops record of completed work and that the vendor had just said compaction has been firing at roughly half the real window - which is the whole reason reconcile-before-building exists as a skill. On-demand compaction changes the shape of the problem: the summary becomes something we author at a chosen boundary and can verify, and the turns carrying proof of completed work can be held verbatim behind it instead of being summarised away by a trigger we do not control. Concretely it is the fix for the pragma-scoring-architecture class of incident - a fix applied to a script that turned out not to be the one running in production - because the record of what was already done survives the boundary. This is now the re-test with the clearest payoff on the list: run one long Hermes/PRAGMA job with an explicit compaction boundary and verify reconcile-before-building finds the prior work on the far side of it.

bullets.title: arXiv REPORTED AS A FINDING RATHER THAN AS "UNCHECKED" FOR THE FIRST TIME IN THREE FIRES - THE DAILY LISTING STILL DOES NOT RESOLVE, BUT SEARCHING THE CORPUS DIRECTLY TURNED UP AN ENTIRE SKILL-LIFECYCLE-GOVERNANCE LITERATURE THAT IS ARCHIVE-ZERO AND IS PRECISELY THE INSTRUMENT ARTIFACT (c) HAS BEEN MISSING FOR NINETEEN DAYS
bullets.summary: The honest label first: none of these is this week's paper. The 2605.x and 2603.x identifiers are months old, the daily listing did not resolve through our fetch layer for a third consecutive fire, and nothing datelined 16-17 Sep surfaced. It is printed because the archive returns ZERO on all five and the subject has an open, aging artifact. The cluster: SkillsVote treats agent skills as having a governed lifecycle - collection, recommendation, evolution; SkillOS learns curation for self-evolving agents; SkillBrew does multi-objective curation of a skill bank; ProcMEM saves reusable procedural memory from past runs without retraining; Evoskill does automated skill discovery for multi-agent systems. Archive grep: SkillOS ZERO, SkillBrew ZERO, SkillsVote ZERO, ProcMEM ZERO, Evoskill ZERO, 2605.06614 ZERO across eighty files.
bullets.how: YES - method for a job already on the board and unstarted. Artifact (c), the skill-corpus audit, has had three instruments and zero runs for nineteen days, and the reason it has never run is that "audit the skills" has no defined output. This literature supplies one: a skill corpus is not a folder, it is a BANK WITH A LIFECYCLE, and the audit's deliverable is a curation decision per skill - keep, merge, evolve, retire - against usage evidence. Our corpus is now large enough that the question is real: this report alone cites verify-before-claiming, review-build-before-claiming-done, gate-measures-defects-not-beauty, reconcile-before-building and the render gates as if each were distinct, and at least two overlap. The cheap version is one pass: list every skill, mark last-triggered, propose merge-or-retire for anything that has never fired. That is artifact (c) with a shape, and it can run without reading a single paper.

bullets.title: STANDING ACTIONS - DAY SEVENTEEN, SECOND FIRE. FOR THE FIRST TIME IN FIVE FIRES THE LIST IS NOT CHARACTER-FOR-CHARACTER IDENTICAL: (b) CHANGED, BECAUSE THE VENDOR SHIPPED THE INSTRUMENT AT 00:12

KILLED ON DATELINE, AND THIS ONE IS THE INTAKE RULE EARNING ITS KEEP: the search layer served OpenAI Presence as a 16 September enterprise-agent-platform launch; the dateline read at the page is JULY 22, 2026 and archive grep puts it in 2026-07-25.md - dead twice over, and it would have been this fire's bullet 3 if the page had not been opened. ALSO KILLED ON PRIOR COVERAGE: Salesforce Agentforce 360 and the seven named agents (11 Sep, archive 2026-09-15); Claude for Financial Advisors (archive 09-15, 09-16); Claude Sonnet 5 introductory pricing made standard - served as current, actually 10 August, Sonnet 5 hits eighteen files. REPORTED HONESTLY RATHER THAN EMPTY: frontier models nothing datelined 16-17 Sep, the dated model index still ends at GPT Image 2.5 (8 Sep), GPT-6 Astra (3 Sep) and Gemini 3.8 Flash (2 Sep), all archived; MCP servers nothing new datelined 16-17 Sep, Docusign's 30 Sep opening remains the next dated event.
bullets.how: YES - and the composition is different from this morning for the first time in five fires: the ecosystem moved three times in ten hours, all three moves were INSTRUMENTS rather than announcements, and two of them landed inside our own tooling.

praxis_lesson: THE FIRST FIRE'S LESSON WAS THAT OUR INDEX LIST CONTAINED THE PLACES THAT REPORT ON VENDORS AND NOT THE PLACES WHERE VENDORS REPORT ON THEMSELVES. APPLYING THAT CORRECTION FOUR HOURS LATER PRODUCED, IN ONE PASS, THE LEAD, THE BEST RE-TEST ON THE BOARD, AND THE LARGEST KILL OF THE WEEK - the lead came from a GitHub releases page, the compaction item from the platform's own dated release notes, and OpenAI Presence died because its own page says 22 July while the search layer sold it as yesterday. A method correction that pays out the same day is rare enough to be named as the day's actual result. SECOND, AND IT IS THE SHARPER ONE: for sixteen appearances item (b) has been carried as a decision we had not made, when the truthful description was that we could not SEE what managed settings resolved to, so there was nothing to decide against. At 00:12 the vendor shipped the telemetry and the item silently changed category from BLOCKED to UNTYPED. A backlog item's excuse can expire without anyone noticing, because nothing in our process re-reads the backlog against the day's releases - the report re-reads the world and the list is copied forward unchanged. That is the same defect as yesterday's DeepMind bullet, one level up: the gates cannot enforce, and the list cannot notice. The cheapest correction is to make the standing list a DIFF rather than a PASTE - each fire, one line per item saying what changed about it, which would have caught (b) at breakfast instead of in a footnote. THIRD, THE ACCOUNT: the day's three real items are a credential leak on our own MCP surface, a $34M bet that certification decays between stamps, and a literature that tells us what a skill audit is for. Two of the three are about knowing what our own agents did and whether they stayed inside their boundaries. We still cannot answer that question about a single one of them, and the artifact that would - (a), the incident log, nine rows of prose - is on its nineteenth day with a ready-made schema sitting in bullet 2 of this morning's file.
